component.name: Gifkino
component.summary: Edit animated GIFs along the time axis

description.p: This package installs the official upstream build unmodified: upstream publishes the application tree from their own Flatpak build as a release asset, and it is unpacked here at install time, not rebuilt. It follows their releases automatically, and is published by Gifkino's own developer.

Gifkino is a GIF editor for Linux built on one idea: an edit knows which frames it applies to. Add a caption once and it spans the range you chose, instead of being retyped on every frame it should cover. Open an existing GIF or import a video, work on the frame list, then export an optimized GIF.

ul.li: Text, shape and image overlays scoped to a range of frames.
Crop, resize, rotate and flip, applied across the whole animation.
Frame list editing: reorder, duplicate, delete, retime.
A timeline that zooms, with overlay bands showing what covers what.
Undo and redo over every edit, including scoped overlay changes.
Video import through ffmpeg, with a frame budget you set before decoding.

description.p: The ffmpeg, ffprobe and gifsicle programs the editor drives come with it, so video import and the optimized export pass work with nothing installed on the host.

Permissions: Gifkino runs with no network access and no static access to your files. Opening and saving go through the file-chooser portal, which grants exactly the file you pick, and settings are kept in the app's own directory under ~/.var/app/io.github.zbcoding.Gifkino. If you would rather hand it a directory outright — a scripted batch, or a file manager that cannot forward a path — enable it with flatpak override:

ul.li: Read and write GIFs in Pictures without the portal: flatpak override --user --filesystem=xdg-pictures io.github.zbcoding.Gifkino
Import clips straight from Videos: flatpak override --user --filesystem=xdg-videos io.github.zbcoding.Gifkino

screenshot.caption: An eight-frame GIF on the canvas with a text overlay, the frame strip and overlay bands below, and the frame and overlay properties on the right

description.p: An About dialog, and the welcome screen leads with the action.
Exports report progress, and overlays copy across frames.
Video import asks how the clip should land, whatever its size.
